newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair hopes for fare hikes in IATA talks.
newsitem.headline: Finnair hopes for fare hikes in IATA talks.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy will up its ticket prices if the International Air Transport Association's (IATA) emergency talks starting on Wednesday lead to concerted hikes, spokesman Usko Maatta said.
"There would be a need to up prices but we are waiting to see if the meeting comes up with a coordinated move," he told Reuters by telephone on Wednesday.
Asked whether Finnair would up prices if IATA decides so, Maatta said "yes".
Scandinavian Airline SAS said on Tuesday it was increasing passenger ticket prices by 2.0 percent and freight prices by 5.0 percent due to higher fuel costs.
Delegates from the world's airlines on Wednesday began a round of emergency meetings in Geneva to discuss strategies to counter a recent surge in fuel prices that is gnawing at their profitability.

IATA said last week at its annual general meeting that airlines were on course for their second straight year of record profits, but a recent rise in jet fuel prices of some 30 percent has forced it to retreat from its April forecast for an industrywide profit of about $6 billion.

Airlines paid an average worldwide price last year of 65.2 U.S. cents a gallon (4.5 litres). The price soared to 77.5 cents in September after the United States fired 27 cruise missiles against Iraq as a warning to Baghdad to comply with Gulf War ceasefire resolutions.
The IATA meeting is expected to last through Friday.
